title: Strict liability — escape of dangerous things

content.heading: Strict liability
content.text: A person who, for their own purposes, brings on their lands and collects and keeps there anything likely to do mischief if it escapes, must keep it in at their peril, and is prima facie answerable for all the damage which is the natural consequence of its escape, without proof of negligence. The rule, received from Rylands v Fletcher, typically requires a non-natural use of land and an escape causing damage. Recognised exceptions include act of God, default of the claimant, consent, act of a stranger, and statutory authority. In hazardous industrial enterprise cases, Indian courts have applied a stricter absolute-liability standard with narrower defences.
